correctness.rationale: Every derivation has unique edge parameters (beta_e,z_e) and the defining Leibniz rule is verified on the basis. Innerness is equivalent to zero signed cycle sum. In a nonzero class the support of (beta=0,z!=0) omits a cycle edge, so signed-incidence rows are independent. Fourier orthogonality gives ((q^2-1)^j-(-1)^j)/q for j active cycle edges in a fixed nonzero class. The resulting polynomial has q^(2m-1) total and q*ell rank-one maps in every nonzero class. The exact standalone checker independently enumerates ranks and solves potential equations for six finite cases including GF(4).

value.rationale: Rank distribution within a fixed nonzero outer-derivation cohomology class is a natural finer invariant than its dimension. The first nontrivial graph-cohomology case (unicyclic height-two posets) has a complete, field-uniform polynomial; rank-one multiplicity q*ell detects the unique cycle length and every positive rank occurs. This supplies a structural and reproducible infinite-family classification beyond mere existence of non-inner derivations.
